summary: Unexpected egress line item on private deployment invoice despite reserved hours covering month
description:
Issue summary: Customer BrightCart Inc. reports an unexpected 'egress' line item (~€1,320) on their finalized March invoice for a private deployment. They assert that the organization's reserved hours contract for eu-west (monthly reserved pool) should have covered the traffic and that egress is included in their enterprise Private plan.

Impact: Finalized invoice shows a large one-time egress charge which has put autopay on hold. Customer finance is requesting an immediate explanation and provisional credit while we investigate. Affects billing for the whole org (all API keys associated with the private VPC connector).

Environment: Private control plane; dedicated private connector in eu-west-1; reserved hours contract active for March; deployment uses partner transit gateway (third-party peering).

What customer saw: Itemized invoice lines show: 
- reserved-hours (applied)
- model usage lines (chat/embedding)
- new line: private-egress: euro-amount 1320.00 (no detailed tag or cost center)

Expected: No egress line (egress was contractualized in their Private plan).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer exports finalized invoice from Console -> Billing for March cycle. 2) Filter by cost-center 'private-vpc-connector' 3) Expand line items and click 'private-egress' line -> shows no origin tags. 4) Support attempted to reconcile postback logs and found egress postbacks tagged as 'hosted' for discrete windows between 2026-03-03 and 2026-03-04.
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: A transient tag-sync failure between Private connector service and billing postback pipeline caused a subset of egress events to be labeled 'hosted' and billed at egress tariff.

What we checked: 
- Reserved-hours ledger shows credit applied for March. Credits reduce model usage lines but do not auto-offset mis-tagged egress tariff lines.
- Postback consumer logs (billing-consumer-02) show consumer restart at 2026-03-03T21:58:30Z, coincident with deploy-bot tagging event.
- Cross-checked network logs in Private control plane: transit gw reported sustained egress for that hour.
- Found one queued replayer job in billing-backfill that failed to map route_tag -> cost_center due to schema change in PR 9f3a4b2 (linked above). That PR was rolled out 2026-03-03.

Intermediate conclusion: Likely regression from recent billing schema normalization deploy (PR 9f3a4b2) that changed route_tag/connector mapping. A fraction of egress postbacks lost connector mapping and fell into default 'hosted' tariff during a 40-minute window.

Next steps planned: 
- Ask Engineering to backfill mapping for 2026-03-03 21:50 -> 22:30 and recompute tariff assignment (ENG-allocator).
- If backfill succeeds, request billing to issue provisional credit and regenerate invoice lines.
- Add an alert to deploy-runbooks to block schema deploys without mapping validations for private connectors.

resolution_notes: Work in progress: Engineering to run backfill and recompute tariff assignments for affected windows. If mapping restored, Billing will issue provisional credit equivalent to the egress line and regenerate invoice lines. Follow-up actions: add pre-deploy validation for route_tag mappings and create a post-deploy reconciliation job to detect missing connector tags within 1 hour of schema changes. Owner for follow-ups: Priya Patel (SRE) and Diego Ramos (Billing Eng).
